question.text: An SIA is scoping an impact assessment engagement and needs to confirm that the donor company is itself CSR-liable under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013. Which of the following threshold sets triggers CSR applicability (any ONE being sufficient)?

answer.text: Net worth >= INR 100 cr OR turnover >= INR 500 cr OR net profit >= INR 2 cr
Net worth >= INR 500 cr OR turnover >= INR 1,000 cr OR net profit >= INR 5 cr
Net worth >= INR 1,000 cr AND turnover >= INR 500 cr AND net profit >= INR 10 cr
Only listed companies with market capitalisation above INR 500 cr are CSR-liable

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 135(1) of the Companies Act 2013 requires every company (including a foreign company) meeting ANY of these criteria in the immediately preceding financial year to constitute a CSR committee and spend 2% on CSR: (a) net worth >= INR 500 crore, (b) turnover >= INR 1,000 crore, or (c) net profit >= INR 5 crore. The trigger is 'any one', not 'all three'. **The Trap:** INR 100/500/2 cr figures are pre-amendment / unrelated thresholds. 'AND' conjunction is wrong — any ONE threshold suffices. Market-cap-based applicability is not part of Section 135. **Cross-Exam Context:** X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) and compliance exams cover CSR scope. XXIII asks the SIA to confirm the donor's CSR eligibility before attributing inflows as CSR in the Impact Report. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Always collect the donor's CSR-2 filing acknowledgement or its Board's CSR policy to confirm applicability. If the corporate slips below the threshold in a given year but continues to give, the gift is a voluntary donation, not a statutory CSR contribution — this distinction matters for your narrative on programme sustainability.
